## Summary

I performed a comprehensive security review of the repository, tracing data flows from HTTP entry points to dangerous sinks and verifying each candidate against false positives.

**3 exploitable findings reported:**

| # | Category | Severity | Location | Root Cause |
|---|----------|----------|----------|------------|
| 1 | SQL Injection | CRITICAL | `src/routes/search.js` → `src/db/search.js` | `req.query.q` concatenated directly into a SQL string; no parameterization → arbitrary read of all DB tables |
| 2 | Insecure Deserialization / RCE | CRITICAL | `src/jobs/import.js` | `req.body.payload` passed to `node-serialize.unserialize()` (CVE-2017-5941) → arbitrary code execution |
| 3 | Hardcoded Secret | HIGH | `src/config/payment.js` | Live (`payment_live_`) payment key committed in source |

**Deliberately excluded as false positives** (verified safe, not pattern-only dismissals):
- `src/files/download.js` — proper path-traversal containment via `startsWith(ROOT + path.sep)`
- `src/process/image.js` — array-form `spawn` with `shell: false` (the documented safe pattern against command injection)
- `src/routes/users.js` — ownership check enforces `req.user.id === req.params.id` (no IDOR)
- `src/db/users.js` — correctly parameterized query
- `src/logging/redact.js` — strips `password`/`token`; not the data flow's trust boundary
- `src/health.js` — intentional trivial unauthenticated health probe

The final machine-readable report is saved to `SECURITY_REVIEW.json` with `source_modified: false`. No audited source files were touched.
